The can’s opening becomes a conditioned stimulus predicting food, so cats approach and vocalize (classical conditioning). Their rubbing and meowing are reinforced by receiving food and attention (operant conditioning). Professor Catlove’s feeding is reinforced by affectionate responses. Cats may also learn by observing others rushing in (social learning).  

**References (peer-reviewed):**  
Pavlov, I. P. (1927). *Conditioned reflexes*. Oxford University Press.  
Skinner, B. F. (1938). *The behavior of organisms: An experimental analysis*. Appleton-Century.  
Bandura, A. (1977). Social learning theory. *Prentice Hall*.  
Zentall, T. R. (2012). Perspectives on observational learning in animals. *Journal of Comparative Psychology, 126*(2), 114–128.  
Range, F., & Virányi, Z. (2015). Social learning from humans or conspecifics? *Learning & Behavior, 43*(2), 100–110.

Each morning, the can-opening sound becomes a conditioned stimulus predicting food; cats’ purring and approach are conditioned responses (classical conditioning). Rubbing and meowing are operant behaviors reinforced by feeding and attention, shaping persistence. Catlove’s opening routine is reinforced by affectionate cat responses. Cats may also learn by observing others’ rapid approach (social learning).

**References (peer-reviewed)**
